steps.thought: I will list the available tests to understand the test suite and their costs.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run power_on_selftest first to quickly check basic communication and enumeration across I2C, UART, and CAN subsystems.
steps.observation: The power_on_selftest passed successfully with all devices on I2C, UART, and CAN buses responding normally and no reported failures.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power on self test passed cleanly, but further subsystem tests are required to confirm health.
No failures yet detected, but comprehensive testing has just begun.

steps.thought: I will run the battery_rest_check to verify battery cell voltages and resting health as the next inexpensive subsystem check.
steps.observation: The battery_rest_check passed cleanly with a pack voltage of 16.6V, healthy cell voltages, and minimal imbalance of 5mV, ruling out battery rest anomalies.

hypotheses.rationale: Both power on selftest and battery rest check passed with no failures, pointing toward a healthy unit.
Remaining subsystems such as ESCs, motors, IMU, and camera still need to be tested.

steps.thought: I need to check the ESC telemetry next to verify motor and ESC health, continuing the systematic subsystem check.
steps.observation: The esc_telemetry test failed due to high packet loss across all four ESCs, indicating a communication issue or telemetry disturbance. Meanwhile, power_on_selftest and battery_rest_check both passed cleanly.

hypotheses.rationale: ESC telemetry shows elevated packet loss and synchronization errors on esc_1 and esc_2.
High packet loss across all ESCs on the CAN bus could point to bus termination or wiring issues.
General packet loss on multiple ESC nodes suggests harness or stub signal degradation.

steps.thought: I will run the harness_continuity test to check the CAN bus termination and stub integrity, as high packet loss on all ESCs points to a potential bus communication issue.
steps.observation: The harness_continuity test failed because the CAN termination resistance was 120.9 ohms, which is well outside the expected range for a properly terminated dual-resistor bus (54-66 ohms), explaining the high packet loss across all ESCs in esc_telemetry.

hypotheses.rationale: Measured CAN termination resistance of 120.9 ohms instead of ~60 ohms strongly indicates a missing second 120 ohm terminator resistor on the bus, causing reflection and high packet loss across all ESC nodes.
While packet loss is high across all ESCs, the bus-level termination measurement failure points specifically to missing termination rather than a localized stub issue.

steps.thought: The harness continuity test definitively showed a CAN termination resistance of 120.9 ohms, which is incorrect for the dual-resistor CAN bus and explains the packet loss on all ESC telemetry nodes. No further tests are needed; I will proceed to propose the rework.
